clue.text: Bird identified by fellows in university

indicators.note: in places the fellows inside the name of the university

parts.note: Yale is a well-known American university
F is the standard abbreviation for fellow, so two fellows give FF

explanation.surface: A bird species named by the dons of a university.
explanation.walkthrough: The yaffle is a country name for the green woodpecker.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect name for the green woodpecker, a British bird with a laughing call.

clue.text: Leads off march with flute and stringed instrument

indicators.note: the leading letters are taken off each of the two words that follow

parts.note: taken as written before losing its first letter
taken as written before losing its first letter

explanation.surface: A band strikes up a march with flute and strings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads off' removes the first letter of both march and flute, leaving ARCH and LUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bass lute with extra unstopped strings, played in the Baroque era.

clue.text: Staff keeping up the standard

parts.note: read not as employees maintaining quality but as a pole that holds a flag (a standard) aloft

explanation.surface: Employees maintaining high quality at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall pole from which a flag, or standard, is flown.

clue.text: A walk to divert and please

indicators.note: diverting the letters sends them on a new route into a different order

explanation.surface: A stroll along the seafront taken for amusement and pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A level promenade for walking, typically along a seafront.

clue.text: Cause of widespread ill-feeling

parts.note: read not as general resentment but as sickness spreading through a population

explanation.surface: Something that makes people everywhere resentful.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak of disease affecting many people at once, making large numbers feel unwell.

clue.text: He led pair astray dreadfully in Eden

indicators.note: something done dreadfully is done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Adam led Eve badly astray in the Garden of Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'dreadfully' does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden is the biblical paradise on earth.

clue.text: Beater familiar with traps and snares

definitions.text: Beater familiar with traps and snares

parts.words: Beater familiar with traps and snares
parts.note: suggests a hunting beater who knows about traps, but traps are a drum kit and snares are snare drums

explanation.surface: A game beater who knows all about traps and snares.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussionist beats drums, and a drum kit is called the traps, including snare drums.

clue.text: Way to speed in the middle of the road

definitions.text: in the middle of the road

parts.note: a way of doing something is a mode
a speed is a rate, as in rate of travel

explanation.surface: A suitable speed to drive at in the centre lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of the road' looks like a place on the road, but it is the idiom for holding centrist views.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-of-the-road views are centrist, avoiding extremes.

clue.text: Composer's beginning with a note to produce musical work

indicators.note: the beginning of the word Composer's is its first letter

parts.note: a oncer is old British slang for a one-pound note
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer starts with a single note to create a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests music, but it is a banknote: ONCER was British slang for a one-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece for a solo instrument with orchestra is a type of musical work.

clue.text: Belligerent type one ceases to employ?

definitions.meaning: someone who scraps things, discarding what is no longer used

explanation.definitionFit: One who scraps fights; one who scraps things throws them away.

clue.text: Strain resulting from difficulty getting back to study

indicators.note: the word for difficulty is turned back to front

parts.note: rub means difficulty, as in there's the rub
a den is a private study or workroom

explanation.surface: Stress caused by struggling to get back to one's studies.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a heavy load or burden, something hard to bear.

clue.text: Hit and run, not taking care

parts.note: to slap is to hit
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: A careless hit-and-run driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Done hastily and carelessly, with no attention to detail.

clue.text: Come out, say, with part of army in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: eg (for example) is introduced by say
REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, is a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A soldier emerges as a unit of the army falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' reverses EG and REME together, giving EMER and GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To come out into view is to appear or surface.

clue.text: Bound by old agreement reached initially in 1996, say

parts.note: a bound is a leap
ye is an archaic form of the

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Tied by an ancient pact first agreed in 1996.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as tied, but it is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: 1996 had 366 days, with February 29 added, as an example of such a year.

clue.text: David and John, for example, in suitable accommodation

indicators.note: the painters are placed inside the word for suitable

parts.note: apt means suitable
Jacques-Louis David and Augustus John were painters, men of art

explanation.surface: Two men named David and John find a suitable place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: The names look like a flatshare, but they are the painters David and John.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a set of rooms used as living accommodation.

clue.text: Beginner or top player said to give up

indicators.note: said tells us the word is heard, not read

parts.note: a seed is where a plant begins, and a seeded player is a top player in a tournament

explanation.surface: A novice or a star player told to throw in the towel.
explanation.walkthrough: SEED covers both senses, and it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up territory or a right is to yield or surrender it.

clue.text: Profit growth?

parts.note: read not as rising earnings but as a plant grown for selling

explanation.surface: A rise in company earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop grown for sale rather than for the farmer's own use, so the growth is literal.

clue.text: Such a creature is around in reconstructed form

definitions.text: Such a creature is around in reconstructed form

indicators.note: a reconstructed thing is put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A prehistoric animal brought back as a museum skeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: Extinct reptiles survive today only as skeletons reconstructed in museums.

clue.text: Put out of service when bishop leaves in protest

indicators.note: when the bishop leaves, its letter is removed

parts.note: to demob is to discharge someone from the armed forces
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman quits his post in protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of demonstration, a public protest march or rally.

clue.text: Outline of French writer

parts.note: de is French for of
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A sketch of a French author.
explanation.definitionFit: To outline something is to give an account of it.

clue.text: Duke goes in to dinner, say, guided with gong

indicators.note: the duke's letter goes inside the word for dinner

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal
led means guided

explanation.surface: A duke is led in to dinner to the sound of a gong.
explanation.walkthrough: The dinner gong is a decoy: 'gong' is slang for a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for a medal or award, so with a gong means decorated.

clue.text: Single out animals about to charge

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the animals are read backwards

parts.note: apes are animals
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Picking out creatures about to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to charge' reads as on the point of attacking; 'about' turns APES into SEPA.
explanation.definitionFit: To single out is to pick apart or set apart from others.

clue.text: Set out to anger with fruitless result

indicators.note: out signals the word set is turned out of its normal order

parts.note: to rile is to anger

explanation.surface: Setting out to annoy someone, with nothing to show for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren, unproductive; land or effort yielding nothing.

clue.text: Unidentifiable gangster seizing one note after another

indicators.note: the gangster word seizes the notes, holding them inside

parts.note: a hood is a hoodlum, a gangster
D and E are musical notes, one following the other in the scale

explanation.surface: A masked gangster grabs one banknote after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The notes go in before the last letter of HOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose face is covered by a hood cannot be identified.

clue.text: Dictator collecting gold to cart off

indicators.note: the anagram collects the gold, picking it up in front

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: off signals the letters go off in a different order

explanation.surface: A tyrant amasses gold and has it carted away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram; 'collecting' only loosely places the gold, which here sits in front rather than inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler with unchecked power, a tyrant.

clue.text: Staff that's including a touring assistant

indicators.note: the word for staff includes the letter a inside it

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
ie (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A staff member who travels with a band as helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A road crew member who sets up equipment for a band on tour.

clue.text: Absurd, having, credit withdrawn — dreadful for consumer.

indicators.note: credit withdrawn means its letters are taken out

parts.note: absurd here means unbelievable
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A bank that withdraws credit is absurd and awful for its customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumer' is one who eats, not a shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that cannot be eaten is dreadful for whoever has to swallow it.

clue.text: Contradictory by-lines

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Bylines in a newspaper that contradict each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrary, deliberately going against what is expected.

clue.text: Fashionable design in check

indicators.note: the design word is placed inside the check word

parts.note: to try is to check or test
an end is an aim or design

explanation.surface: A stylish checked pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' and 'check' look like fabric patterns; they are END (an aim) and TRY (a test).
explanation.definitionFit: Up to date, in vogue, following the latest style.
